title: Etale maps into a finite henselian local unramified target lift uniquely
statement: Let R be a commutative local ring, S an etale R-algebra [def-weil-etale-morphism], and T a module-finite formally unramified R-algebra that is henselian local [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. Writing k for the residue field of R, the map Hom_R(S,T) to Hom_k(k tensor_R S,k tensor_R T), f maps to id_k tensor f, is bijective. R need not be henselian and S need not be module-finite.

source.place: Tag 04GG, condition (8) and proof of (1) implies (8), applied over T; Tag 04GK full faithfulness local-target case; Tag 00UW (1) for m_R T=m_T. Sources checked online at the corresponding Stacks tag pages.

proof.text: A finite algebra T over a local ring R has all maximal ideals over the maximal ideal of R. Since T is henselian local, its structure map is local. By Mathlib Algebra.FormallyUnramified.map_maximalIdeal, m_R T = m_T. Identify k tensor_R T with T/m_R T by quotIdealMapEquivQuotTensor, then with the residue field l=T/m_T by quotientEquivAlgOfEq. Extend scalars along the surjective residue map R to k to get a k-algebra equivalence e. On 1 tensor t it is the residue of t.

For an etale algebra C over a henselian local T and a T-algebra map chi:C to l, let q=ker chi. The map chi is surjective since it restricts to the surjective residue map of T; q is maximal and its contraction is m_T. The induced residue map from the residue field of T to that of q is injective as a field homomorphism. It is surjective: represent an element by c in C, choose t in T whose residue is chi(c), and use c minus the image of t in q. Apply the existing unique pointed etale retraction theorem at q. Its retraction sigma reduces exactly to chi by the same c minus t argument. Any lift tau of chi has inverse image of m_T equal to q, so uniqueness gives tau=sigma.

Base change S to C=T tensor_R S; C is etale over T. TensorProduct.liftEquivRight identifies maps S to T with T-algebra maps C to T, and maps S to l with T-algebra maps C to l. A reduced map k tensor_R S to k tensor_R T, followed by e and restricted to S, yields such a point C to l. Lift it uniquely by the previous step and transport back to an R-algebra map S to T.

For injectivity, equality of two reduced maps implies equality of the residues of their values at every s, by applying e to 1 tensor s. Tensor induction shows their corresponding T-algebra maps lift the same point; uniqueness of the lift and injectivity of tensor adjunction give equality. For surjectivity, apply the residue-lifting identity to 1 tensor s. It proves equality of the lifted reduction and the given map on those elements. k-linearity gives equality on a tensor s for any a in k, and tensor induction gives equality everywhere. This includes the zero source; a zero target is excluded by HenselianLocalRing T.

proof_origin.place: Q1 adaptation of the unique retraction criterion, Tag 04GG (8), to maps with a finite local target; the tensor adjunction and reduction identification are explicit Lean proofs.
